body:
ORIGIN: GitHub issue #137, dogfooded on #104/PR #135. This ticket is self-contained; the issue is background only.

PROBLEM (evidence): Across the opencode T30-T35 arc AND #104, every real correctness/security bug was caught by a cross-model (codex/GPT) adversarial pass ONLY AFTER same-model ADLC P5 prosecution returned a clean SHIP. In #104 same-model P5 passed the security-critical half as airtight, yet codex then found two real bugs (an add-only writer/gate mismatch, and completed-ticket backlog pollution). Root cause: a same-model prosecutor validates the author's own tests, which encode the author's blind spot. ADR-0007 (docs/adr/0007-multimodel-adversarial-review.md) establishes cross-model review but only as RECOMMENDED practice, so it depends on the operator remembering to run it. For trust-root / deny-path / gate-producer changes that is too load-bearing to be optional.

GOAL: For a defined high-risk tier, a clean P5 is IMPOSSIBLE without a recorded cross-model adversarial `approve` from a DISTINCT provider. Convert the recurring lesson from discipline-I-apply into a gate that blocks.

DELIVERABLES:
1. Trust-root-tier classifier. Implement in packages/prosecute (NOT packages/core, which is frozen per CONVENTIONS rule 2; note core/lib/risk-tier.mjs is a DIFFERENT concept — model frontier/direct/ladder tiers). Classify a change (its changed-file set, derivable from a git diff against a base ref, plus the target ticket's scope/rails) as trust-root tier iff it touches any of: scripts/rails-guard-ci.mjs, docs/ci/rails-guard.yml, scripts/test/rails-guard-workflow-hashes.json, .adlc/tickets.json, a package that emits an exit-2 gate, a declared rail/deny path, or is a producer of a gated artifact (a tool that writes .adlc/tickets.json or a manifest). Deterministic, offline, unit-testable.
2. Cross-model attestation in the manifest. Define a manifest entry type (e.g. type "cross-model-review") recorded via packages/gate-manifest with data { provider, verdict, baseRef, ticket }. The adversarial-review tool already emits a verdict (exit 0 = approve); wire a record step (a documented `gate-manifest record cross-model-review --data ...` invocation, or a thin helper) so the attestation is machine-checkable. Do NOT trust a provider string the author can freely forge into an approve without having run a review — at minimum bind the entry to the reviewed baseRef/revision so a stale attestation against an old diff does not satisfy a new one (mirror how prosecute already binds revisions).
3. Gate it in prosecute. packages/prosecute/lib/run.mjs already reads the manifest (readEntries) and gates P5 on "three distinct dry lenses recorded". Extend it: when the change under prosecution is trust-root tier, P5 additionally requires >=1 cross-model-review approve entry from a provider DISTINCT from the authoring/same-model reviewer, bound to the current revision. Missing -> exit 2 with a clear message naming what is required. Non-trust-root tier: behavior unchanged (no regression).

CLAUDE CODE PLUGIN: plugins/adlc-claude-code — the adlc:prosecutor agent is same-model by default. After a same-model SHIP on a trust-root-tier change it must SURFACE "same-model P5 passed; this tier requires a cross-model pass" and offer the one-command cross-model invocation (it can shell to the local `codex` CLI). Update the P5 text in plugins/adlc-claude-code/skills/adlc/SKILL.md accordingly.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (each with a concrete verification):
- AC1: The tier classifier returns TRUE for a diff touching each enumerated trust-root/gate/deny/producer surface and FALSE for an ordinary feature diff (e.g. a docs-only or single-app-file change). VERIFY: node --test with positive AND negative fixtures for every surface class.
- AC2: gate-manifest can record and read a cross-model-review attestation carrying provider, verdict, and the reviewed baseRef/revision. VERIFY: node --test round-trips a recorded entry and reads it back; an attestation bound to a stale revision does NOT satisfy the current one.
- AC3: adlc prosecute exits 2 for a trust-root-tier change with no matching cross-model attestation, and exits 0 once a distinct-provider approve bound to the current revision exists; a same-provider (non-distinct) attestation does NOT satisfy the gate. VERIFY: node --test exercising all three branches with fixtures.
- AC4: A NON-trust-root-tier change is unaffected (prosecute outcome identical before/after this ticket). VERIFY: a regression test on an ordinary change.
- AC5: Docs updated — extend docs/adr/0007-multimodel-adversarial-review.md from "recommended" to "gated for the trust-root tier"; update docs/toolkit.md step 6 and the P5 section of plugins/adlc-claude-code/skills/adlc/SKILL.md. VERIFY: grep the updated language; the phase-router drift test (scripts/test/router-drift.test.mjs) stays green if the skill is generated.
- AC6: full root `npm test` exits 0; `adlc rails-guard` passes for this ticket's diff.

RAILS NOTE: rails intentionally left [] at authoring. Declaring rails now would freeze packages/prosecute/** and packages/gate-manifest/** in CI for ALL PRs until this ticket completes (rails have no start-lifecycle), blocking unrelated work. Declare the real rail set (e.g. freeze the prosecute + gate-manifest test files being made load-bearing) at P3 when the build actually starts.

OUT OF SCOPE: editing packages/core/** (frozen); building the adversarial-review tool itself (external repo voodootikigod/adversarial-review); the risk-tier taxonomy beyond the binary trust-root-tier decision (finer tiers are a follow-up).
title: Gate cross-model adversarial review for the trust-root risk tier (make ADR-0007 a P5 gate, not a recommendation)
